title: Own twelve-piece band at the Club Congo
summary: Leading a twelve-piece show band at Detroit's Club Congo, he writes for headline acts and makes good money, with personnel named.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional

blocks.x: When did you take your own band into the Club Congo?
This is what I'm coming to right now. I went into the Club Congo. It was a good band, too. But I came through there, and Hamp changed my mind about the whole situation.
How did he do that?
Well, he offered me a job! Ha-ha. I figured... I said, what I'm gonna do is either stay here and work in this joint... And it was really a good job. I mean...
Well, you had a 12-piece band, I understand.
A 12-piece band. Yeah, it was nice.
And you wrote for the band?
Yeah.
And you had the show?
Yeah, we played for the shows.
And played for dancing and the whole thing?
Yeah. But Hamp persuaded me to give that up and come with him.
But what kind of place was the Club Congo?
It was just a joint where people go and drink and dance and so forth, and they put on the show twice a night.
Like with a shake dancer and a comedian and the whole thing?
Yeah. Mills Brothers and all them...
Oh, you had some headliners.

All the headliners came in, yeah. Well, I made a fortune out of the club, because most of the acts that came in, they didn't have no music, and they had to have music. So I would write for... You know, I would tell them, 'Well, I'll write the music for you' and charge them so much for it, you know. So I made a fortune... Like, I did very good in that club.
How long were you at the Congo, would you say?
About six months. Maybe a little longer than that, I don't know. But anyway...
Who was in the band? Anybody that we would know?
Well, let's see. I don't know whether you would know these people or not. Let's see. Johnny Young
played piano...
Not the one that's in Chicago.
Oh, no...
A different John Young.
This is a different John Young. Let's see. Well, I don't think you'd know any of these guys. Most of them was from Detroit. You know Kelly Martin.
Yeah. He was the drummer.
Yeah, he was the drummer. And we had... I'm trying to think it was we had on tenor. Wardell came in after I left, but they had another tenor player there. Okay... Where did I go from there...?
